summary: The (5,2)-cycle cover conjecture -- that every bridgeless graph has a 5-cycle double cover -- remains open as of September 2026, but the chart on this page moved: the July 2026 proof of the cycle double cover conjecture (OpenAI/GPT-5.6; exposition arXiv:2607.16356) gives every bridgeless graph an (8,2)-cycle-cover (Theorem 18), and hence an (m,2)-cycle-cover for every $m \ge 8$. Between 5 and 8 the question is open. Earlier partial progress on the (5,2) case includes Hoffmann-Ostenhof's characterisation of when a 2-regular subgraph of a bridgeless cubic graph extends to a 5-cycle double cover, and verification for several snark families via nowhere-zero 4-flow methods.

since_posted.title: A proof of the cycle double cover conjecture by OpenAI: An exposition
since_posted.claim: Theorem 18: every bridgeless graph has an 8-cycle double cover, i.e. an (8,2)-cycle-cover, obtained directly from the new proof of the cycle double cover conjecture (the construction uses the seven nonzero elements of $\mathbb{F}_2^3$ plus padding). This fills a previously unresolved box of the (m,n) chart on this OPG page. The conjecture asked on this page -- the (5,2) case, i.e. the 5-cycle double cover conjecture of Celmins and Preissmann -- is explicitly restated as open (Conjecture 20).

since_posted.title: A note on 5-cycle double covers
since_posted.claim: Establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for a 2-regular subgraph of a bridgeless cubic graph to be containable in a 5-cycle double cover, advancing the strong 5-CDC conjecture.

notes: Two further post-2007 papers were found in search results but could not be accessed via WebFetch (journal paywalls/redirects): (1) Liu, Hao, Luo, Zhang, '5-Cycle Double Covers, 4-Flows, and Catlin Reduction', SIAM J. Discrete Math. 37(1):253–267, 2023, DOI:10.1137/22M1472425 — verifies 5-CDC for several snark families using Catlin reduction; (2) Zhang, 'Five-cycle double cover and shortest cycle cover', J. Graph Theory 108:39–49, 2025, DOI:10.1002/jgt.23164 — studies 5-CDC for weak-oddness-2 cubic graphs. arXiv:2511.07285 (approximate CDC, 2025) addresses general CDC but not specifically the (5,2)-cover. The (5,2)-cover conjecture is strictly stronger than the CDC conjecture, which is itself still open. 2026-09-06 update: the cycle double cover conjecture itself is now a theorem (OpenAI/GPT-5.6, July 2026; exposition arXiv:2607.16356). Consequently the confirmed implication (5,2)-cycle-cover => CDC recorded in data/relations.json is now vacuous, and the honest statement of what this page still asks is: close the gap between the (8,2)-cover that is now a theorem and the conjectured (5,2)-cover.
